terms.comment: An ancient noun applied to sand play.

phrases.latin: ventus ē specū ērūpit, lūmina appāruērunt
phrases.english: a wind burst out of the tunnel, lights appeared

phrases.latin: Per cunīculum trānsīmus; mox lūx redībit.
phrases.english: We’re going through the tunnel; the light will soon come back.
two scouts were sent through the tunnel

phrases.latin: nihil illō carcere longius, nihil illīs facibus obscūrius, quae nōbīs praestant nōn ut per tenebrās videāmus, sed ut ipsās
phrases.english: nothing longer than that prison, nothing dimmer than those torches, which let us see not through the darkness but the darkness itself (the tunnel at Naples)

sources: Lewis & Short: specus · Lewis & Short: cuniculus
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 203, 219, 399.

Theodōrus et pater · Ad Larem avītum, Libellī I–VII, as they stood on 7 November 2026, with their glosses. Examples marked “Libellus” quote those texts word for word; classical passages are cited by author.
